claims.text: The wear resistance and microscopic deformation of a FeNiCrCoCu coating during high-temperature sliding are governed by formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline or dynamically amorphized near-surface layer.
The near-surface layer develops from a coarse-grained starting microstructure.
The baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating is single-phase and coarse-grained.
Slight grain coarsening or alteration of the defect structure by heat treatment enhances the coating's predisposition for shear-induced dynamic recrystallization.
Thermally activated dynamic recovery and recrystallization are active under the intended high-temperature sliding conditions.
The sliding-induced ultra-nanocrystalline or amorphized surface layer mediates plastic deformation.
Accumulated surface plastic deformation triggers shear-induced dynamic recrystallization or amorphization.
The ultra-nanocrystalline layer accommodates strain through grain-boundary-mediated sliding.
The ultra-nanocrystalline layer distributes stress more uniformly.
Formation of the ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer reduces friction and wear.
The pre-treated coating will form a more extensive ultra-nanocrystalline surface layer than the baseline coating.
The pre-treated coating will have a lower wear rate than the baseline coating.
The pre-treated coating will exhibit more homogeneous and less localized plastic deformation than the baseline coating.
The untreated baseline forms only a limited ultra-nanocrystalline layer and consequently exhibits greater localized wear and deformation.
The proposed mechanism should dominate at high temperatures where thermal activation assists dynamic recrystallization.
The proposed mechanism may not govern at low temperatures.
In strongly oxidizing atmospheres, oxidative wear may prevail over the proposed near-surface-layer mechanism.
The role of Cu in changing the threshold grain size and kinetics of dynamic amorphization in FeNiCrCoCu is not quantified.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism present ultra-nanocrystallization and amorphization as alternatives, whereas the structural mediator describes one layer as both ultra-nanocrystalline and dynamically amorphized. A fully amorphous layer is not simultaneously nanocrystalline without specifying a mixed or spatially differentiated structure.
